contentHtml:
A client requests GET /health from NGINX and receives 502 Bad Gateway. In this lab the intended path is client → 127.0.0.1:18080 (NGINX) → 127.0.0.1:18081 (backend). The exercise reproduces two causes of the same upstream connection error. Use the backend process and its listening socket to choose the repair.

Set up a local Linux lab

Use three Bash terminals on the same Linux machine, as the same regular user in the same network and PID namespaces. The observer runs all diagnostics. The proxy and backend terminals each own one foreground service. Use NGINX with the standard HTTP modules and the -e option, Python 3.7+ with http.server, curl, ss (iproute2) and ps (procps). All three ports bind to loopback. The backend serves one synthetic file.

In the observer terminal, check the ports before starting. Expect no rows. If a port already has a listener, use another lab environment.

ss -H -ltn '( sport = :18080 or sport = :18081 or sport = :18082 )'

From the repository root in the observer terminal, create a private directory for this run. Copy the printed cd command into the proxy and backend terminals.

lab=$(mktemp -d)
cp examples/operational-scenarios/network-and-tls/reverse-proxy-502/nginx.conf "$lab/"
mkdir "$lab/site"
printf 'booking-backend-ok\n' > "$lab/site/health"
printf 'cd %q\n' "$lab"

In the proxy terminal, after changing directory, validate and start the supplied NGINX configuration. Its PID, logs and temporary files are relative to this lab prefix. Leave it running for both faults.

nginx -e stderr -p "$PWD/" -c nginx.conf -t &&
  nginx -e stderr -p "$PWD/" -c nginx.conf

In the backend terminal, after changing directory, define the following function and start the server. The subshell records its PID, then exec starts Python under that same PID. Wait for its serving message before each probe. Ctrl+C in this terminal stops just this foreground service.

serve() (
  printf '%s\n' "$BASHPID" > backend.pid
  exec python3 -m http.server "$1" --bind 127.0.0.1 --directory "$PWD/site"
)
serve 18081

Record a healthy request

In the observer terminal, define the client request once. It prints the HTTP status and body even for a 502. Use this same request after each repair. Confirm the destination in the config used to launch the proxy.

probe() {
  curl --noproxy '*' --silent --show-error --max-time 3 \
    --output "$lab/response" --write-out 'HTTP %{http_code}\n' \
    http://127.0.0.1:18080/health && cat "$lab/response"
}
grep 'proxy_pass' "$lab/nginx.conf"
probe

Expect proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:18081; and the following response. Start fault injection only after both the status and body match.

HTTP 200
booking-backend-ok

Collect evidence for each 502

Define this function in the observer terminal. It takes a log position before the request so the second fault cannot reuse the first fault's error line. The PID file holds the identity of the last launched backend. Compare it with the command in ps and the PID in the socket's users: field. An empty ss result means neither backend port has a TCP listener.

inspect_fault() {
  local previous_lines backend_pid
  previous_lines=$(wc -l < "$lab/error.log")
  probe
  tail -n "+$((previous_lines + 1))" "$lab/error.log"
  backend_pid=$(cat "$lab/backend.pid")
  printf 'Recorded backend PID %s\n' "$backend_pid"
  ps -p "$backend_pid" -o pid=,stat=,args= || echo 'No process at recorded PID'
  ss -H -ltnp '( sport = :18081 or sport = :18082 )'
}

Fault 1 — the backend stopped

  1. Press Ctrl+C in the backend terminal and wait for its shell prompt.
  2. Run inspect_fault in the observer terminal. Expect HTTP 502 and an NGINX error page. The fresh error log should contain connect() failed (111: Connection refused) while connecting to upstream and upstream: "http://127.0.0.1:18081/health". The recorded PID is gone and the socket query returns no rows.
  3. In the backend terminal, run serve 18081. In the observer terminal, repeat probe. Record HTTP 200 and booking-backend-ok before starting the second fault.

Fault 2 — the backend is listening on the wrong port

  1. Press Ctrl+C in the backend terminal. Run serve 18082 and wait for its serving message.
  2. Run inspect_fault in the observer terminal. Expect the same 502 and a new connection refusal for 127.0.0.1:18081/health. This time ps shows a live python3 -m http.server 18082. The ss line for 127.0.0.1:18082 shows that process's PID. There is no listener on the configured upstream port, 18081.
  3. Correct the backend launch port. Press Ctrl+C in the backend terminal and run serve 18081. In the observer terminal, repeat probe and record HTTP 200 and booking-backend-ok.

In a rehearsal on Ubuntu 24.04 with NGINX 1.24.0, the following observations distinguished the two failures. PIDs vary by run.

Observation Backend stopped Backend on the wrong port
NGINX error for this request Connection refused on 127.0.0.1:18081 Connection refused on 127.0.0.1:18081
ps for the recorded backend PID 1179696 absent PID 1179713 running http.server 18082
ss for the two backend ports No listener PID 1179713 listening on 127.0.0.1:18082
GET /health through the proxy after repair 200, booking-backend-ok 200, booking-backend-ok

If the process, socket and fresh error line disagree, preserve those observations and the client response before making another change. On a shared service, hand them to the proxy and backend owners. In a containerized deployment, inspect the listener in the backend's namespace and test reachability from the proxy's namespace. Each has its own loopback address when the two use separate network namespaces.

Clean up

Press Ctrl+C in the backend and proxy terminals and wait for both shell prompts. In the observer terminal, run the socket check again. After confirming it returns no rows, remove the private directory created for this run.

ss -H -ltn '( sport = :18080 or sport = :18081 or sport = :18082 )'
rm -r -- "$lab"

For the operating standards, see Networking and Edge and the network incident runbook. NGINX documents how it forwards the request to the selected upstream, and the Linux socket tool documents how it displays the owning process. NGINX proxy_pass and ss(8).
